topic: Funding a Marketing Push Without Draining Cash
objective: Explain how finance can support a marketing investment without straining working capital.

slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: A significant marketing push can pay off, but paying for it entirely out of working capital can leave little room for the day-to-day. Financing the campaign separately — with a facility sized to the expected return — keeps growth spending from crowding out operations.

caption:
A bigger marketing push often needs bigger upfront spend before the return shows up — which is exactly the kind of timing gap finance is suited to. Funding it separately, rather than draining working capital, keeps the rest of the business running normally while the campaign plays out.

The key is sizing the facility to a specific, considered campaign — not an open-ended spend.
